Aimed strikes

Choose an aimed strike to target a body part.

Small targets are harder to hit. Wounds to different body parts have different effects.

Controls depend on your keyboard, gamepad and camera settings. The in-game guide shows your current bindings.

Classic edition reference

These original pages describe classic mouse and keyboard controls. Use the guidance above for current settings and gamepad controls.

Backstab

Your blows will cause much greater damage if you can catch your enemy unawares and strike him. To perform a "backstab" your character must get close to the enemy from the behind without him noticing (its best to use the "Sneak" mode so the enemy won't hear you), and then strike him before he realizes what's happening.
If your enemy notices you approaching and switches to Aggressive mode, your blow will not be counted as a "backstab". So be sneaky!

Precision blows

When you order your character to attack an enemy you can specify what body part he should aim at. Use the following keypad keys for precise blows:
<4>: aim at left hand (left fore leg)
<6>: aim at right hand (right fore leg)
<1>: aim at left leg
<3>: aim at right leg
<5>: aim at body
<8>: aim at head

To land a precise blow, hold the appropriate key down, and place the cursor over the enemy. Your character will aim right at the specified body part until you issue a different command or until the health of this body part reaches 0. If the enemy is still alive, additional blows will not be precise ones.

Some of the beings in the game have no arms or legs. If you issue a command to aim at a nonexistent body part your character will just ignore it.

All characters' body parts can be protected by armor which has specific "armor" properties - so the damage inflicted on such protected body parts reduced.

Aim at limb

If your character loses an arm, he will attack and cast spells much more slowly. A character loses an arm when the arm's health reaches 0. You can see this in the Information window if it's switched to "Hit locations" mode.
If your character has lost a leg, his/her movement will be much slower. A character loses a leg when the leg's health falls to 0. You can see this in the Information window if it's switched to "Hit locations" mode.

Head blow

Head blows are considered critical. They cause three times more damage than other blows. However, the chances of striking the head are much lower than other body parts.
